event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: COVID-19 first hit more than four years before TPR’s August 2024 filing, so the pandemic has shifted from an acute shock to a medium-term, structural risk.  The company’s language shows that management still regards COVID-19 as a live threat: they treat it as both a historical fact that has already hurt operations (especially in Greater China) and as an ongoing source of potential disruption to supply chains, store traffic, labour availability, liquidity and capital-market access.  However, the disclosures are largely qualitative and un-quantified.  They catalogue many operational vectors (store closures, inventory build-ups, labour shortages, excess promotions, etc.) but stop short of giving fresh dollar figures.  Notably, management also states that FY-2024 results were *not* materially affected, signalling partial recovery.  Under the Time Decay Principle, a 4-year-old event can still command moderate scores (4-6) when a filer provides specific, multi-faceted risk statements, but generic or mitigated references must be scored more conservatively.  Overall, COVID-19 remains a material, yet now moderated, risk factor for TPR: the pandemic’s legacy vulnerabilities persist in supply chains and consumer behaviour, but the immediacy and severity have ebbed since 2020-2022.

evidence_list.snippet: Public health crises, such as the Covid-19 pandemic, may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

components.reason: Explicitly names Covid-19 as a risk driver.
Identifies multiple material impact areas (business, financial condition, operations, cash flows).
Forward-looking wording ('may adversely affect') signals continuing exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, forward-looking statement tying COVID-19 to core financial metrics warrants the upper end of medium-term scoring.

evidence_list.snippet: Widespread public health crises, such as the Covid-19 pandemic, have had, and could in the future have, a negative impact on our operations, cash flow and liquidity.

components.reason: Acknowledges both historical and prospective impact ('have had, and could in the future have').
Specifies critical areas—operations, cash flow, liquidity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combines backward-looking evidence of damage with future risk across multiple financial dimensions, justifying a top-range medium score.

evidence_list.snippet: Potential risks to our business include but are not limited to: (i) disruption of our supply chain; (ii) loss or disruption of key manufacturing or fulfillment sites; (iii) closures, operating restrictions and capacity restrictions at our stores and our ability to negotiate existing lease agreements; (iv) changes in consumer shopping behavior, including reduced discretionary spending; (v) costs associated with adhering to regulations and protecting the health and safety of our employees and customers, (vi) excess inventory leading to increased promotional activity, (vii) heightened competition for retail and fulfillment center employees, (viii) our ability access capital markets and to make payments on and refinance our debt obligations; and (ix) our ability to pay dividends or conduct stock repurchases.

components.reason: Provides a detailed, nine-point catalogue of operational and financial pandemic-related risks.
Covers core pandemic-sensitive areas (supply chain, consumer demand, labour shortages, liquidity).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly specific enumeration of COVID-linked vulnerabilities, but absence of quantification keeps score mid-range.

evidence_list.snippet: Our results can be impacted by a number of macroeconomic factors, including but not limited to: consumer confidence and spending levels, tax rates, levels of unemployment, consumer credit availability, pandemics, natural disasters, raw material costs, fuel and energy costs, bank failures, market volatility, global factory production, supply chain operations, commercial real estate market conditions, credit market conditions and the level of customer traffic in malls, shopping centers and online.

components.reason: Includes 'pandemics' among macro factors affecting results.
Statement is generic and grouped with many other factors, diluting specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Only a broad, catch-all reference; still relevant but relatively weak evidence yields a low-moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: The Covid-19 pandemic has resulted in varying degrees of business disruption for the Company since it began in fiscal 2020 and has impacted all regions around the world, resulting in restrictions and shutdowns implemented by national, state and local authorities.

components.reason: Confirms actual, historical disruption beginning in 2020.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates concrete historical harm and worldwide reach, but purely backward-looking, hence a mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: During fiscal 2024, the Covid-19 pandemic did not materially impact our business or operating results.

components.reason: Explicitly states no material impact in the current year, signalling mitigation.
Still references pandemic context, so risk not fully eliminated.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Current-year mitigation offsets the generic risk relevance; under Time Decay this produces a neutral net score.
